title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Arena on 1971-04-12
lineage: SBD > Reel Master > DAT > Sound Forge > CD > EAC > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Crisp sound‑board capture of a high‑energy April ’71 Pittsburgh show, highlighted by a smoking Other One, epic Lovelight and tight Phil bass work.
ai_review.review: The recording is an exceptionally clear SBD source that puts the band up close—vocals and instruments are crystal‑clear though the audience is barely audible.  Musically the concert is a standout for 1971, with a blistering second set (Other One → Lovelight, Not Fade Away → Greatest Story → Playing in the Band) and strong Pigpen, Garcia and Phil performances, despite a few tape‑flip cuts that truncate songs like Hard to Handle.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating across ~20 detailed reviews is ~4.3; the vast majority praise both performance and sound quality, with only occasional notes of cuts or minor glitches.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very crisp, close‑miked SBD mix; vocals and instruments sit front‑and‑center. Audience is almost inaudible (a common SBD trait). Reviewers note occasional jumpy spots, tape‑flip cuts (e.g., Hard to Handle) and a few glitches in Cold Rain & Snow, but overall the sound is clear and balanced.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Greatest Story Ever Told > Playing In The Band
poor_songs: Wharf Rat (described as a work in progress)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts a bit shaky but tightens by Bertha; second set opens strong with Truckin' and a powerful Other One, flows through seamless segues into Lovelight and the NFA → GDTRFB sequence.  Tape‑flip cuts interrupt a few jams, but overall pacing is high‑energy and well‑structured.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia is described as firing up, delivering strong guitar riffs and vocal presence (though occasional lyric slips on Loser).
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly praised – ‘Phil in high gear’, ‘prominent Phil zone’, ‘totally in charge tonight’.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for tightened rhythm work; drives Hard to Handle and Johnny B. Goode, with strong guitar presence throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann gets special mention for a white‑hot performance on Lovelight and overall tight drumming.
